source_name: Smith et al. Journal of Small Animal Dentistry
source_quote: Toy breeds showed significantly higher periodontal burden than medium controls.
Patellar luxation prevalence remained elevated across toy lineages.
Small breeds had higher chronic pruritus and atopic diagnoses.
Small-breed airway collapse remained a frequent chronic morbidity.
Medium dogs showed measurable but lower hip dysplasia prevalence than large dogs.
Medium-sized cohorts had persistent otitis incidence in humid climates.
Large-breed dogs demonstrated significantly higher hip dysplasia prevalence.
Large dogs had higher non-contact cruciate rupture rates.
Giant and deep-chested dogs showed increased lifetime GDV prevalence.
Giant breeds developed earlier and more severe osteoarthritic change.
